chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from his father, with his chain of narrators, which he ascribed to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,
that he said to a man from his companions: Do not be a flunky who says: «I am with the people» or «I am like (any) one of the people».

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.أَصْحَابِهِ: His companions, referring to the close followers of the Imam.
key_terms.إِمْعَةً: A flunky or follower who lacks independent conviction, often used pejoratively for someone who merely echoes the crowd.

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'im'ah' mean in Shia hadith and how does it relate to social conformity?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s warning against the 'im'ah'—a person of weak conviction who lacks independent judgment and merely conforms to the majority for social ease. This concept is central to Shia ethical discourse, distinguishing between *talfiq* (pragmatic following) and *ittiba'* (following the truth), urging believers to cultivate *istiqama* (steadfastness) even when standing alone against prevailing trends.
